title: mysql_instance.py start()/init-start reports false STARTED when port 3307 is occupied by an unrelated, pre-existing WAMP MariaDB service
reproduction_steps: Independent check: mysql.exe -h127.0.0.1 -P3307 -uroot -e 'SELECT VERSION(), @@datadir, @@port' returned '11.4.9-MariaDB' / 'c:\\wamp64\\bin\\mariadb\\mariadb11.4.9\\data\\' / 3307 -- NOT MySQL 8.4.7

Root cause found in the tool's own mysqld.err for that init-start attempt: the real 8.4.7 process logged 'Can't start server: Bind on TCP/IP port' and 'Do you already have another mysqld server running on port: 3307 ?', then aborted and shut down cleanly at 09:29:57Z -- yet the tool's stdout still reported STARTED, because start() only polls `mysqladmin ping` on the target host:port, which succeeds against ANY MySQL-protocol server already listening there, not specifically the process it just spawned

Confirmed via Get-CimInstance Win32_Service: 'wampmariadb64' (MariaDB 11.4.9, C:\wamp64\bin\mariadb\mariadb11.4.9\bin\mysqld.exe) is a genuine, independently-running WAMP Windows service bound to port 3307, State=Running

MariaDB's own error log (KILSYSTEM-SG.err) shows a single 'Starting MariaDB ... as process 16416' entry at 2026-09-17 13:55:03 with no subsequent shutdown entries -- i.e. running continuously since BEFORE all three Wave5 commits (7f9a7dd/abcb762/edf0d41, all dated 2026-09-18)

Decisive corroboration: mepa_wave3_test_pool_01, mepa_wave4_test_pool_01, mepa_wave4_test_pool_02 (the exact synthetic pool database names tools/test-infrastructure/pool.py creates) already existed on this MariaDB service before this audit touched port 3307 at all -- these can only have been created by an earlier `pool.py create-and-migrate --port 3307` run whose migrate_pool_db.php subprocess connected to whatever was actually listening on 3307 at that time, which -- given the continuous MariaDB uptime since 2026-09-17 -- was almost certainly this same shared, non-disposable service, not a genuinely isolated per-session MySQL 8.4.7 instance

discriminating_test.purpose: Determine whether a PHPUnit run hitting this collision could still produce the documented clean result
discriminating_test.probe: CREATE TABLE t (id INT, v INT, CONSTRAINT ck_v CHECK (v >= 1)); INSERT INTO t (id,v) VALUES (1,0); -- against the MariaDB service on 3307
discriminating_test.result: ERROR 4025 (23000): CONSTRAINT `ck_v` failed -- MariaDB's CHECK-violation error code, NOT MySQL's 3819
discriminating_test.significance: apps/api/tests/Database/WaveFivePhysicalTest.php:165-207 hardcodes `self::assertSame(3819, ...)` for all 6 CHECK-violation cases. Had the claimed 'OK (7 tests, 2272 assertions)' PHPUnit run actually executed against this MariaDB service, that assertion would have failed loudly (4025 != 3819), which is inconsistent with a clean pass. This does not prove the original A1 run avoided the collision (this audit cannot time-travel to confirm), but it does prove the harness provides no way to distinguish a trustworthy MySQL 8.4.7 run from this failure mode without an independent VERSION()/error-code cross-check, which nothing in the automated pipeline (pool.py, migrate_pool_db.php, WaveFiveCase.php, the validators) performs.

adr_0014_five_criteria_assessment.b_cannot_produce_false_PASS: FALSE -- demonstrated: init-start itself returns a false STARTED status; by extension anything built on 'STARTED means a genuine dedicated MySQL 8.4.7 instance is ready' inherits that false-positive risk
adr_0014_five_criteria_assessment.c_cannot_hide_a_real_failure: FALSE -- demonstrated: the real mysqld 8.4.7 bind failure was completely hidden behind {"status":"STARTED"}
adr_0014_five_criteria_assessment.d_cannot_damage_another_runs_resources: FALSE -- demonstrated: mepa_wave3_test_pool_01/mepa_wave4_test_pool_01/02 persist on a shared, always-on service rather than a disposable per-session instance, meaning separate 'isolated' test sessions on this machine are not actually isolated from each other
adr_0014_five_criteria_assessment.e_cannot_invalidate_critical_evidence: NOT RULED OUT -- cannot be proven false given available evidence; the collision was standing throughout the entire Wave5 implementation window
adr_0014_five_criteria_assessment.conclusion: Does NOT qualify for TEST_INFRA_DEBT (fails b, c, d as demonstrated, not merely theoretical). Classified as EVIDENCE per ADR-0014.

workaround_used_for_this_audit: Re-ran all live tests against port 33071 (confirmed free) instead of 3307. Independently verified VERSION()=8.4.7 before trusting the instance. All fresh/upgrade/rollback/remigrate/FK/UNIQUE/CHECK/concurrency evidence in this audit's own report was gathered against this verified-correct instance, not the colliding MariaDB service.
recommended_remediation: mysql_instance.py's start()/init-start must verify, after mysqladmin ping succeeds, that the responding server is (a) the specific process it just spawned (PID/datadir match, same technique stop() now uses per P0.3.5-A1.0) and (b) reports the expected MySQL 8.4.7 version string -- failing closed (STARTED -> BIND_FAILED or similar) rather than trusting a bare ping. This is the mirror-image of the stop() false-success bug already found and fixed in P0.3.5-A1.0; that fix did not cover start().
